analysis.title: The Commodities Feed: Brent builds geopolitical premium as Gulf risks rise
key_insights: Front-month ICE Brent settled 4% higher at just above $113/bbl on 22 October. ING says the rally reflects supply concerns about the Persian Gulf, not current fundamentals.
Reports say President Trump is considering fresh strikes on Iran, the US is deploying a second aircraft carrier to the region, and US troops have been evacuated from some Middle East bases.

ING says these developments call into question its long-held view that the US midterm elections would bring de-escalation and normalisation in flows and prices. It sees re-escalation as the most likely path.
ING's expectation of ICE Brent averaging $80/bbl in 4Q26 is looking unattainable. Even without re-escalation, the possibility of it is likely to keep a sizeable geopolitical risk premium in prices.
TTF gas rose 3% to settle above EUR90/MWh, the highest since December 2022. LNG flows are increasingly likely to be largely absent from the market for much of the Northern Hemisphere winter.
EU gas storage appears to have peaked at just under 75% full and fell marginally on Tuesday.

Spot gold fell 2.8% to near $4,000/oz and did not benefit from the equity sell-off or the drop in the US 10-year yield to below 5%. The market is focused on higher oil prices feeding inflation and tighter central bank policy.

LME copper fell more than 1.9% for a second straight session on rising exchange inventories and an AI-related stock sell-off. Inventories rose 27,675 tonnes for a fourth consecutive session to 272,950 tonnes, the highest since 27 July 2026.

sector_views.rationale: ING expects a sizeable geopolitical risk premium to stay in oil and European gas prices because of Persian Gulf escalation risk.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The yield fell back below 5% during the equity sell-off, but gold did not benefit.
ING says this forecast now looks unattainable given Gulf escalation risks.

risk_factors: Renewed US-Iran escalation in the Persian Gulf could disrupt oil flows that have so far stayed resilient.
LNG flows may be largely absent from the market for much of the Northern Hemisphere winter.
Higher energy prices could intensify US inflation and strengthen the case for tighter monetary policy.
Rising LME copper inventories and an AI-related stock sell-off weigh on risk sentiment.
